ImageDescription.value:
Logbook, kept by two keepers, comprised of two voyages. First voyage documents the Montgomery (Ship) of New Haven, mastered by Trowbridge, kept by Jeremiah Townsend III, from 29 January 1784-3 April 1784. Not whaling, pp. 359-399. New Haven to Londonderry, Ireland. MS fair copy made by Thomas R. Trowbridge Jr., 1880s. Second voyage documenst the Neptune (Ship) of New Haven, mastered by Daniel Greene, kept by Ebenezer Townsend, from 1 January 1797-11 July 1799. Sealing voyage, pp. 5-357. South Pacific Ocean, Hawaii, and Canton (China). MS fair copy made by Thomas R. Trowbridge Jr., 1883.

• Scope and content: This series consists of various records. Most of the materials relate to people in one, or both, of two categories: Axis personnel accused of committing war crimes, or of belonging to criminal organizations, during World War II; and former Axis personnel who were used by the U.S. or West Germany as intelligence sources during the Cold War. The series also includes files relating to people who were never accused of war crimes or of belonging to criminal organizations, but who may have been associated with war crimes as victims, witnesses, investigators, sources, or officials.
